newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Waterford, Avonmore shareholders to vote on merger.
newsitem.headline: Waterford, Avonmore shareholders to vote on merger.

text.p: Farmer shareholders in Waterford Foods Plc and Avonmore Foods Plc meet later on Friday for a decisive vote on a proposed merger between the two groups.
Shareholders must ratify or reject the merger which would create the largest dairy company in Britain and Ireland and the fourth largest milk processor in the world.
To succeed, the merger needs the support of 75 percent of farmers attending two consecutive extraordinary meetings.
The first meeting was held on July 11 and 83.2 percent of Waterford shareholders voted in favour of the merger while 97.6 percent of Avonmore members approved it.
Both second meetings are scheduled to begin at 1200 local time (1100 GMT) and results are expected mid-afternoon.

Almost 3,200 Waterford shareholders attended the first meeting but Waterford's management has expressed concern that a lower turnout might jeopardise the final endorsement of the deal. They have appealed to farmers to turn out in force again today.

Opposition to the merger has focused on the reduction of farmer control of the new company to 55 percent from 67 percent and opponents have also warned that the merged group might not necessarily continue to pay a better milk price.
But Waterford chief executive Matt Walsh says the merger proposal offers a compelling business logic and is the ideal strategic response.
"In the rapidly changing commercial environment for the dairy sector of the 1990s, there are major benefits in participating in a larger and stronger business structure," he said.
Avonmore and Waterford have a joint turnover of 2.5 billion Irish pounds ($3.7 billion) and pre-tax profits of 71.5 million.

Analysts said the merged company's milk production would far outstrip the dairy operations of Britain's Northern Foods Plc and Unigate Plc and its cheese production would account for 20 percent of the British market.
